name: Ireland

observations.reasoning: Sourced on 2026-07-27, transversal pass over the population indicator. Population on 1 January 2025: 5440278 inhabitants, recorded as 5.44 million. Eurostat dataset demo_pjan, Population on 1 January by age and sex, read through the dissemination API on 2026-07-27, dataset last updated 2026-07-09. Total population, both sexes, all ages, which is exactly what this indicator's denominator asks for. Read as one table covering every country in the record, so no value here is derived from a neighbour: each is that country's own row. The previous value was an opening estimate produced with no source and no research.

Searched on 2026-07-27, in English, in the transversal venues pass. Zero, and it is a recent zero: Ireland had a puppet theatre with a building and lost it. The Lambert Puppet Theatre at Monkstown, County Dublin, was set up in 1972 by Eugene Lambert and run after his death in 2010 by his son Liam; an arson attack in August 2015 did more than 150 000 euro of damage, it reopened that November with rebuilt puppets, and it closed permanently in 2018. It would not have counted in any case on the reading this record uses — the article describes it as a family-run business, and no public backing appears — but its closure is why the question has no other candidate. Irish puppetry today works as companies rather than houses, and a funded company without a venue is excluded by the denominator by name. Recorded open rather than verified because the Arts Council's list of funded organisations was not read: that is the check that would show whether any puppetry company has since acquired a room. The previous value was 1, an opening estimate produced with no research, and it was almost certainly counting the Lambert from memory, four years after it shut.

Web check of 2026-07-27, searched in the country's own language. No establishment retained. The only Irish provision identified is the Puppetry Performance Weekend Workshop at the Lir Academy, the national drama school attached to Trinity College Dublin: a weekend workshop covering hand, object, rod, tabletop, moving-mouth and bunraku puppets. A short workshop, even run by a university institution, is not degree-granting higher education and does not satisfy the denominator. Puca Puppets also runs professional workshops, out of scope for the same reason. Upper bound raised from 0 to 1. Estimate, resting on search summaries.

DISPUTED. First value produced as a mean conditioned on artists who actually tour, which drops from the denominator the makers who do not perform. Method error identified: a fee is not a performance. For France the true median probably sits between 10 and 20, over a bimodal distribution. For countries with permanent companies, recomputed from the top: 250 to 400 performances a year, casts of 3 to 5, a company of about twenty, so on the order of 50 to 90. To be redone in full once the denominator is settled.
